method.used: HOST ARMS, unresolvable WS RPC host. Two daemons run from the two release trees on this machine, each with its OWN --data-dir (hence its own socket) under the session scratchpad. NEITHER is the launchd service: no launchctl, no install.sh, no shared data dir, and the launchd daemon stayed LIVE and serving throughout.
method.severMethod: --rpc-ws-url wss://ws-does-not-resolve-kamilens.invalid, with the JSON RPC and Kamigaze URLs left at their working defaults. NO host DNS change, NO /etc/hosts entry, NO firewall rule - any of those would also have cut the live launchd daemon and the play session on it.
method.whyThisIsolatesBetterThanAnOutage: The 0.5.1 failure shape is a JSON provider that ANSWERS beside a WebSocket provider whose socket never opens. A network outage produces that shape transiently; an unresolvable WS host produces it as a constant, with every other input held fixed. The control arm therefore reproduces the reported wedge without any timing luck.
method.dockerOutcome: ABANDONED after three failed builds of the 0.5.2 image. Each died inside the image's npm ci with npm's own 'Exit handler never called!' - an npm bug, not a repo one, and one that EXITS ZERO while leaving node_modules half-installed, so the build only failed two steps later at 'tsup: not found'. The control image built (from cache) and reported 0.5.1 correctly; the fix image never completed within the session's budget. Recorded rather than retried indefinitely.
method.limitation: The RECOVERY half is NOT reproducible by this method and was NOT observed. ensureNetworkIsUp requires BOTH providers to answer, so a permanently unresolvable WS host means 0.5.2 cannot reach LIVE either - what it demonstrates instead is that the failure becomes BOUNDED, COUNTED, SURFACED and LOUD rather than silent and indefinite. 'time-to-LIVE after the network returns' is therefore null here, not zero, and stays unmeasured until the Docker namespace method can run.

fix.preLiveStallVisibilityNote: The degraded string is observable only in the <=5 s window between crossing PRELIVE_STALL_MS and the watchdog tick that resets the progress marker - a 1 s dense poll caught it three times (91s/92s/93s) while the 20 s sampler never did. A real narrowness, predicted at design time and recorded rather than hidden: the string is a bonus signal, and the reliable pre-LIVE signals are state != LIVE and the NOT_READY code on every world read.
fix.finding: Bounded, counted, surfaced and loud. Every WS probe times out at NETWORK_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS instead of hanging forever (33 observed), so the ladder advances; the pre-LIVE watchdog fired 3 times at 90/90/94 s and routed each restart through the SAME onFailed schedule, whose delays escalated 5s -> 15s -> 30s exactly as BOOTSTRAP_RETRY_DELAYS_MS specifies. Every world read answered NOT_READY carrying the state and percentage. status carried feedsDegraded.
fix.countingNote: watchdogRestarts counts only the '... - restarting bootstrap' lines. The same phrase also appears inside each 'bootstrap attempt N failed (pre-LIVE stall: ...)' line, because the watchdog's synthesized reason is quoted verbatim by the retry handler - a naive grep double counts, and did on the first pass.
